inputs: Anchor: VDOT 44.0, from the 2026-05-06 time trial in the profile.
Reclaim ceiling: VDOT 49.8, from the lifetime best in the profile; fitness held before comes back faster.
Trajectory: rate 0.109 per month, responsiveness 1.24, fitted to the log (the Banister model).
Running hours: 7.0 h a week, the hours a week the profile says you can train (7.0 h). The log's last eight weeks average 3.9 h.
Weeks kept: 100%; the planned week is multiplied by it before the forecast, so 75% of 7 h is asked as 5.25 h.
Bodyweight: 81.4 kg, weighed 2026-06-15; the ruck lines read through it.
Home altitude: 300 m; run times are corrected for it.
Selection date: 2027-01-11; each gate is due the number of weeks before it that its standard is meant to be in hand.
assumptions: Running lines are asked of the Banister trajectory from VDOT 44.0 at 7.0 h/week (100% of 7.0 h kept), split the way the model would advise; the spread is the fit's covariance plus its residual.
Rucks are read through the load-carriage model at the current bodyweight; a timed twelve-mile in the log would outrank it.
Every other line is a straight line through its own dated readings (3+ over 42+ days), with the regression's prediction interval as the spread.
A gate's chance is the product of its lines', as if independent. They are not, so it is a floor, and it covers only the lines that could be forecast.
Each gate's date counts back from the selection date by the weeks its standard is meant to be in hand.
